payload.name: Preserve All Enumerated Attributes
payload.description: When a message explicitly lists multiple distinct reasons, preferences, or attributes for a memory, use this Skill to ensure extraction and CRUD keep every listed item instead of truncating to a subset.
content: When extracting a memory from a message that explicitly enumerates multiple distinct components (e.g., 'because of A, B, and C'), preserve all components; do not drop any item to shorten the candidate.
If the enumerated list is long, split it into multiple compact memories rather than omitting any item.
When updating an existing memory with newly stated enumerated details, add every missing component rather than updating only a subset.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed failure is an extraction summarization that dropped one explicitly stated trait from a compound reason, leaving an incomplete preference memory. The reusable mechanism is that explicit enumerations of reasons, preferences, or attributes are atomic: if the evidence lists multiple items, none may be omitted during candidate extraction or later CRUD. This applies to any future message where a user states a comma-separated list of qualities or motives; it does not apply when the source itself is an intentional paraphrase or general summary.

payload.name: Preserve explicit enumerated items in memory extraction
payload.description: Use when drafting memory candidates from statements that list multiple distinct attributes, reasons, preferences, or items; ensure every listed element is kept in the memory content.
content: When a source message explicitly enumerates multiple distinct facts (separated by commas/conjunctions), preserve each listed element in the candidate memory content; do not paraphrase away any of them.

Before committing an ADD/UPDATE/MERGE, check the candidate against the source enumeration and append any missing elements; if a memory already exists with a partial list, update it to include the full enumeration.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed mechanism is extraction-level loss of enumerated items when a paraphrase collapses a list (e.g., only one of several explicit rewards is kept). This rule repairs that by requiring all enumerated elements to survive into memory candidates. It applies to any future extraction or update of memories about preferences, reasons, outcomes, or other multi-item statements; it does not apply when the source is not an explicit list.

payload.name: Preserve direct quotes in memories
payload.description: When extracting or updating memories, if a message contains a speaker's direct quote or notable verbatim statement, preserve its exact wording in the memory content instead of only a paraphrase.
content: During extraction, when a message contains a direct quote or notable statement from a speaker, include the exact or near-verbatim wording in the memory content, not just a paraphrase of the event or relationship.
During updates and enrichment, when a new direct quote from a speaker appears in the direct messages, add the quote to the updated memory content so the verbatim statement remains retrievable.

candidates.solves: Future questions that ask what a speaker said fail when constructed memories store only paraphrased summaries and drop direct quotes. This rule is a valid abstraction of that mechanism, and applies during extraction and enrichment whenever a message contains a notable verbatim statement; it does not apply when no substantive quote exists.

payload.name: ExtractExplicitNamedItemsDuringExtraction
payload.description: When a message contains both an activity and a specifically named object, accessory, or clothing item, use during extraction to ensure the named item is recorded even if a broader activity memory is updated.
content: When extracting from a user message that includes both an ongoing activity and a named object/accessory/clothing item (especially one given in answer to a direct question), create a candidate that records the named item, either as a separate memory or as an explicit clause in the activity memory.

Before accepting an UPDATE or MERGE that summarizes a broader activity, check whether the source message explicitly names any concrete item not represented in the proposed content; if so, add it or create an additional candidate rather than letting the broader summary subsume it.
Do not skip a detail solely because it appears in the same sentence as other activity details; each explicitly named noun or attribute is independently extractable.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes omit an explicitly named object or accessory that is the direct answer to a question, because the candidate focuses on a broader activity from the same message. This rule requires named concrete entities to be preserved even when enriching an activity memory. It applies whenever a user message contains both an activity summary and a specific object/accessory named in response to a question; it does not apply to inferred or subjective details.
